samples.summary: Scope creep: hostile-input hardening of `safeFormat` goes beyond the originating issue (#845, decimal round trip). The issue and `docs/tasks/active/20260818-sheets-decimal-round-trip-todo.md` are entirely about making Increase/Decrease reversible; the delta additionally adds a three-tier `Intl` fallback chain (locale → options → bare number → `String(value)`) that also swallows bad currency codes and bad locales, neither of which `changeDecimals` can produce. The `dp` clamp itself is justified (Increase could now push `dp` past Intl's range), but the currency/locale degradation is unrelated hardening riding along in a bug-fix PR — it deserves its own change and its own doc line, and as written it makes any future genuine `Intl` misuse silently invisible.
samples.evidence: safeFormat now has three nested try/catch tiers; the accompanying tests ('should not throw on a currency code Intl rejects', 'should not throw on a locale Intl rejects') test paths the decimal feature cannot reach.

samples.summary: The design doc states as fact that "`Intl.NumberFormat` accepts 0–20 fraction digits and raises a `RangeError` outside that". Since ES2023/ECMA-402, `minimumFractionDigits`/`maximumFractionDigits` are accepted up to 100 on current engines (Node 20+, modern browsers), so the documented rationale for capping user Increase at 20 is inaccurate and the cap is a product decision (matching Google Sheets' limit) rather than a platform constraint. Either restate the rationale as a deliberate product cap or raise the bound; as written the doc records a platform fact that the runtime does not support.
samples.evidence: docs line 292-299 and format.ts:10-14 both assert the 0–20 RangeError rule as the reason for MAX_DECIMAL_PLACES.

samples.summary: `renderedDecimals` re-implements, in a second place, the knowledge of how many decimals each `nf` renders (numeric formats → stored `dp` else 2; plain/date/none → the value's own precision). `formatValue` already owns that rule, and the two must stay in lockstep or `selectionRendersAt` will disagree with what the grid paints — e.g. adding a new `NumberFormat` (or changing currency's default) requires editing both. Deriving the count from `formatValue`'s output (or extracting the per-format decimal rule into one helper both call) would keep a single source of truth. Note also that for `nf: 'date'` it reports the raw value's decimals even though a date render shows none, which is the drift this duplication invites.
samples.evidence: format.ts:152-161 duplicates the default-of-2 and per-format semantics encoded in formatValue (format.ts:182-221).

samples.summary: `clampDecimals` is exported but has no consumer outside its own module (sheet.ts imports only `MAX_DECIMAL_PLACES`, `decimalsInValue`, `formatValue`, `renderedDecimals`; no test imports it; it is not re-exported from `packages/sheets/src/index.ts`). Unless a caller is intended, it should stay module-private to avoid widening the public surface of the format module.

finding.summary: Headline outcome ("Increase then Decrease leaves the cell exactly as it started") is knowingly not met for grouped values and user-chosen `nf: 'number'`
finding.evidence: The task doc's outcome is absolute: "Increase decimal places followed by Decrease decimal places must leave a cell exactly as it started — including leaving no dp/nf behind" (docs/tasks/active/20260818-sheets-decimal-round-trip-todo.md:3-5). The implementation's `unsetKeepsRendering` gate means any value ≥ 1000 (`1234.5`) keeps a `{dp, nf:'number'}` residue after an equal number of increases/decreases — asserted as intended by the new test 'should keep the grouping separators the step would flatten' (packages/sheets/test/sheet/decimals.test.ts:96-113) and recorded as a 'Known deviation' in the todo (:87-89) and in sheet-style.md:262-266. The deviation is documented and argued for, but it is a partial fulfilment of the stated outcome rather than the outcome; a reviewer/verifier should confirm the deviation was accepted on the issue (#845) and not just self-granted in the task file.

verdict.reason: The claimed code and docs are present exactly as described. The todo's headline outcome is absolute (20260818-sheets-decimal-round-trip-todo.md:3-5), and Sheet.changeDecimals only restores inheritance behind the unsetKeepsRendering gate (sheet.ts:4216-4234, 4289-4317), which by construction refuses the unset for grouped values under nf:'number' and for a user-chosen nf:'number', leaving a {dp, nf:'number'} residue after equal increase/decrease counts. That residue is locked in as intended by decimals.test.ts:94-112 and :114-127, and recorded as a deviation in the todo (:87-98) and sheet-style.md:222-232, 266-281. The only candidate refutation ground is already-guarded via the todo's own 'Accepted deviation' paragraph (:7-14), but that text sits in the in-tree task file the change authors maintain, and the finding's core question is whether the relaxation was accepted on issue #845 or self-granted; the issue body is not available to me and #845 appears in the repo only in these same task files, so I cannot establish an authoritative external guard. Spec-conformance against the issue's stated outcome is this lens's lane, so out-of-scope does not apply either. Unresolvable uncertainty means the finding stands.
